name: North Birmingham (Collegeville, Harriman Park, Fairmont and nearby), Birmingham, AL
rule_out: none (stability 0.875; consider trimming southern tracts across I-65)
hook: Worker housing built beside coke ovens and pipe plants that kept the pollution after the jobs left and became the 35th Avenue Superfund site.

name: Greene County and western Black Belt (Eutaw, Boligee, Forkland; Hale, Sumter and Noxubee edges), AL/MS
rule_out: none (crosses into Mississippi; consider trimming to Greene and Hale)
hook: Best Black Belt fit: the county that elected Black local government in 1969 as white families left for a 1965 segregation academy, after a century of out-migration.

name: Perry County (Marion, Uniontown), rural Dallas County (Craig Field) and Brent, Bibb County, AL
rule_out: Bibb Correctional Facility in tract 01007010009; patchwork of three counties, Selma not included
hook: Trimmed to Perry County, a Black Belt place that took 4 million cubic yards of TVA coal ash after Craig AFB (1977) and Judson College (2021) closed nearby.

name: Eufaula, Clayton and Union Springs (Barbour and Bullock, AL) with Quitman and Randolph counties, GA
rule_out: Ventress (tract 9502) and Bullock (tract 9522.02) state prisons in cluster; four counties, two states
hook: A Chattahoochee border region where Eufaula mills closed in waves (2007, 2011) beside plantation counties that gained state prisons.

name: Elizabethtown, Dublin and northern Bladen County, NC
rule_out: none (mill closure dates and job counts still thin)
hook: Best textile fit: a stable-tract county seat that lost its yarn and apparel mills (about 1,000 jobs 2002-2006) and now depends on the Tar Heel pork plant, with Chemours PFAS upstream.

name: Grier Heights, Charlotte, NC
rule_out: none (gentrifying; overlaps U054 as a second Charlotte pick)
hook: A freedmen's settlement outside Charlotte that turned to rentals and 1990s drug crime and now sits in the path of fast gentrification.

name: Tryon Hills / Druid Hills / Camp North End area, Charlotte, NC
rule_out: none (same city as U022; Double Oaks public housing is in neighboring tract 0050)
hook: A North End neighborhood built around one factory site (Ford 1924-1932, Army missile plant, Rite Aid warehouse) and a 1950 public housing project, now remade by Camp North End.

name: Bennettsville (south and east side), Marlboro County, SC
rule_out: split 2010 tract with no 1990 match; older mill history thin
hook: A mill town whose last big textile employer, Mohawk, closed in 2022 with 600 jobs, long after the main wave.

name: North side of Moultrie, Colquitt County, GA
rule_out: split 2010 tract with no 1990 match; thin neighborhood documentation
hook: A small-city neighborhood tied to a packing plant (Swift, 700 jobs at its 1950s peak) that closed in 1996 and later returned under National Beef.

name: Lakeland, Lanier County, GA
rule_out: Patten Probation Detention Center in tract; split 2010 tract; no documented decline events
hook: Little that separates it from many small south Georgia county seats.

name: Many and Fisher, Sabine Parish, LA (Black side of Many plus the old 4L sawmill village)
rule_out: none; 9% group quarters (120 jail, 147 nursing); thin link between parish timber/Toledo Bend history and this neighborhood
hook: A cutover longleaf pine company-town parish where the Toledo Bend reservoir (1963-1969) flooded riverbank Black and Choctaw-Apache communities.

name: Minden's Black neighborhoods, Doyline/Camp Minden, and north Bienville Parish (Gibsland, Arcadia, Ringgold), LA
rule_out: none; sprawling 8-tract mix across two parishes (3 tracts are in Bienville, not Webster); consider trimming to the 3 Minden tracts
hook: A WWII ammunition plant that carried the local economy for 30 years (7,800 jobs in 1967, 1,700 by 1979) left a Superfund site and a 2012 explosives crisis that forced Doyline's evacuation.

name: Stilwell and surrounding Cherokee communities (Zion, Marietta, Lyons Switch), Adair County, OK
rule_out: none
hook: A majority-Cherokee area at the end of the Trail of Tears, lowest per capita income in Oklahoma by 1960, whose strawberry-and-cannery economy faded.

name: South and east Guthrie, Logan County, OK (possibly including The Elbow; Langston not included)
rule_out: unidentified 409-person noninstitutional group quarters in tract 600200 (14%); tract link to The Elbow unconfirmed
hook: A former state capital that lost the capital in 1910, and whose Black creekside neighborhood, The Elbow, was emptied by repeated floods by the 1980s.

name: Okemah, Okfuskee County, OK (Creek Nation; Boley is NOT in this tract)
rule_out: none; note it is Okemah, not the all-Black town of Boley
hook: A Creek Nation county seat that boomed on 1920s oil, had 77% tenant farms in 1935, lost population through 1960, and then faced the 1980s oil bust.

name: El Segundo Barrio and the Chamizal neighborhood, South-Central El Paso, TX
rule_out: none; tract 003602 neighborhood unconfirmed and may not belong; 352-person shelter-type group quarters in tract 002100
hook: The country's immigrant front door on the border, cut by 1916 demolitions, Paisano Drive (1946), I-10 and the Chamizal relocation of about 5,600 people (1963-1968), then hit by a 92% loss of El Paso apparel jobs from 1990 to 2019.

name: Northeast-central El Paso next to Fort Bliss (likely Pershing/Government Hill, unconfirmed)
rule_out: thin documentation; overlaps with stronger U028
hook: A working-class Hispanic area beside Fort Bliss with no documented neighborhood history found.

name: East-side Athens, Henderson County, TX (neighborhood name unconfirmed)
rule_out: boundaries shifted since 1990 (stability 0.507); thin tract-level documentation
hook: An East Texas furniture and TV-cabinet town whose Harvey Industries plant went bankrupt in 1992 and left a state Superfund site.

name: Central and east Mexia, Limestone County, TX
rule_out: Mexia SSLC main campus geocodes to tract 9702, not this tract; but 165 people in nursing group quarters here are unidentified; boundaries shifted (0.636)
hook: A town that jumped from about 3,500 to tens of thousands in the 1921 oil boom, needed 47 days of martial law in 1922, and lost the boom within a few years.

name: Part of Flour Bluff, south Corpus Christi, TX (NOT Hillcrest)
rule_out: not Hillcrest (it is Flour Bluff next to NAS Corpus Christi); no 1990 tract match (stability 0.0); no decline history found
hook: A Navy-base-adjacent area annexed in 1961 with an unexplained very low health ranking; Hillcrest should be pulled as a separate candidate if wanted.

name: Amani, Park West, Franklin Heights and north Lindsay Heights (ZIP 53206), north side of Milwaukee, WI
rule_out: none
hook: Families pushed north by 1960s freeway clearance arrived just as factory jobs began to vanish, and the area became the city's most studied case of male joblessness and incarceration.

name: North St. Louis (The Ville, JeffVanderLou, St. Louis Place, Carr Square) plus two East St. Louis, IL tracts
rule_out: cluster crosses the river into East St. Louis, IL; drop the two Illinois tracts
hook: Repeated rounds of public planning (Mill Creek displacement, Pruitt-Igoe, the 1979 closing of Homer G. Phillips Hospital, and land cleared for NGA West) layered on one neighborhood.

name: West and southwest side of Rockford, IL
rule_out: none (tract 17201002600 has about 579 people in the county jail; consider dropping it)
hook: A machine-tool city that led the nation in unemployment in 1982, split by race along the Rock River, where a 1989 federal suit found the schools had segregated the west side on purpose.

name: Northeast Independence, MO (tract 114.05; neighborhood name unconfirmed)
rule_out: piece of a larger 1990 tract; one tract of 1970s rental apartments; thin documentation
hook: An inner-ring suburban pocket of 1970s apartments in the city once called the meth capital of the world.

name: Charleston, Mississippi County, MO (Bootheel)
rule_out: none (overlaps R028 and R022; best single Bootheel pick; the state prison is not in this tract)
hook: The town where the 1939 sharecroppers' roadside demonstration is marked, hit again when the 1995 shoe plant closing took the factory jobs that had replaced farm work.

name: East Prairie, Mississippi County, MO (Bootheel)
rule_out: too similar to R021 (same county, same cotton history, weaker anchor)
hook: A cotton town inside the Mississippi's managed flood system, shaped by the 1937 flood, an unfinished levee gap and the 2011 Birds Point levee blast.

name: Pemiscot County Bootheel (Caruthersville, Hayti) plus tracts in Lake County TN, Fulton County KY and New Madrid County MO
rule_out: spans 3 states; Tiptonville tract has 2,062 prisoners and a Hickman tract has 471 more (about 11% of the cluster); cut to the 3 Pemiscot tracts or fold into R021
hook: A county that lost two-thirds of its people since its 1940 peak, with a 1995 shoe plant closing and a 2006 tornado stacked on the farm labor collapse.

name: Rocky Ford, Otero County, CO
rule_out: none
hook: A melon and sugar beet town whose sugar plant closed in 1979 and whose ditch water was sold to Aurora in 1987, drying up about 7,500 acres by contract rather than by drought.

name: South-central Hutchinson, Reno County, KS (just south of downtown)
rule_out: thin documentation tying city events to this tract; 117 people in correctional group quarters (4.5%)
hook: The old core of a salt and rail town where a century of abandoned brine wells let a gas leak explode under downtown in 2001.

name: Carmi, White County, IL
rule_out: thin documentation (no dated oil decline or local plant closings found)
hook: A county seat built up by a 1939 oil boom and later tied to one large coal mine that closed in 2016 with about 300 workers.

name: Martin County, KY and lower Tug Fork (Inez, Warfield, Kermit WV, Harts, Chapmanville area)
rule_out: spread across 2 states and 4 counties; overlaps R007 and R003 (pick one Tug Fork/coal story)
hook: The county LBJ used as the face of the War on Poverty in 1964 had a 306-million-gallon coal slurry spill in 2000, and its water system still loses about half its water today.

name: McDowell County coalfields, WV (Welch, Kimball, Gary, War, Iaeger area)
rule_out: tract 54047954503 holds FCI McDowell (1,881 incarcerated, about 11% of cluster pop); drop that tract, the rest stands
hook: The classic one-mineral, one-buyer county lost about four-fifths of its people over 70 years: mine mechanization, then U.S. Steel's exit from Gary, floods, a prison and the loss of its only big grocery store.

name: Williamson and upper Tug Valley (Williamson, Matewan, Delbarton WV; Phelps KY; Hurley VA)
rule_out: too similar to R007 and R019; spans 3 states
hook: A county seat hit in turn by the Mine Wars, the 1977 record flood that walled in its downtown, and 20.8 million opioid pills shipped to two of its pharmacies.

name: East and South Wheeling, Benwood WV, and Bellaire OH (Upper Ohio Valley)
rule_out: none (small pop 8,582; spans WV and OH)
hook: A river valley that lost its steel mills, then its glass works, then its hospital in 2019, after I-70 had already cleared East Wheeling's Black business district.

name: Indianapolis northeast side, 30th-38th St corridor (Forest Manor, Avondale Meadows, Arlington Woods)
rule_out: none (HOLC grades and nearby plant closures unconfirmed; oldest_tract_year 1980 needs a check)
hook: A postwar suburb inside the city limits that fell behind when Unigov merged the city and county but kept the school district lines, followed by 35 years of one-way busing.

name: Austin, Indiana (Scott County)
rule_out: none (single tract, noisy; risk of reading as one event unless the pre-2015 job losses are documented)
hook: A cannery town that lost factory jobs and then had a 2015 HIV outbreak from injection drug use, with 188 cases in a county that usually saw about five a year.

name: Albion, Michigan (Calhoun County)
rule_out: none (Albion College is not in these tracts per 2020 group quarters; 2 tracts, noisy; mid-period dates unconfirmed)
hook: A small foundry town that recruited Black workers from Pensacola in 1916, lost its foundry in 2002 and its high school soon after, while the college on the hill stayed.

name: Flint north-central and east side (I-475 corridor, former St. John Street and Buick City area)
rule_out: none
hook: The neighborhood cleared in the 1960s-70s for I-475 and a Buick expansion, next to the plant that closed in 1999, and then the water crisis in 2014.

name: Flint west side (Civic Park, Chevy in the Hole/Kettering area, Flint Twp edge)
rule_out: too similar to U013 (stronger Flint candidate)
hook: GM built Civic Park in 1919 for its workers and sold it only to white buyers, and the houses outlived the jobs they were built for.

name: Saginaw east side (Saginaw, MI)
rule_out: none (overlaps the Flint auto story; east-side renewal and HOLC history unconfirmed)
hook: Saginaw lost its 12 GM plants one at a time from 1983 to 2014, and by 2020 its homicide rate (50.2 per 100,000) was above Detroit's.

name: Planeview, southeast Wichita, KS
rule_out: none
hook: Federal war housing built in 1942-44 for Boeing workers and meant to be torn down after the war; it never was, and it became Wichita's poorest immigrant gateway.

name: Northern Cheyenne Reservation (Lame Deer, Busby, Birney) plus Decker area, MT
rule_out: weaker than R046 and R006; series takes at most one reservation; this is Northern Cheyenne, not Crow
hook: A nation that walked home from Oklahoma, won its reservation by executive order, then fought off coal leases on more than half its land while coal surrounded it.

name: Browning, Blackfeet Reservation, Glacier County, MT
rule_out: runner-up to R046; series takes at most one reservation
hook: The Blackfeet lost their mountain front to Glacier National Park and land to allotment, and Elouise Cobell from Browning sued over a century of mismanaged trust money.

name: North Havre / Havre North, Hill County, MT
rule_out: thin documentation; one railroad cut in 1992, partly reversed in 1997
hook: A Great Northern division town where Burlington Northern cut 190 shop jobs in 1992 and brought about 100 back five years later.

name: Uptown south and South Central Butte, MT
rule_out: tract is a piece of a 2010 tract with no 1990 match; 10% group quarters (100 correctional, 186 college)
hook: Anaconda's home neighborhood lost its company, smelter and half its people, then lived beside the Berkeley Pit through a 30-year Superfund cleanup of its own attics and yards.

name: Pine Ridge village, Wounded Knee and Wanblee (Pine Ridge Reservation) plus St. Francis and Mission (Rosebud Reservation), SD
rule_out: none; strongest reservation pick, but cluster joins two nations; recommend redrawing to the four Pine Ridge tracts (OLC 9410, 9411; Jackson 9412; Bennett 9412)
hook: The county with the lowest life expectancy in IHME's series every year since 1980, on land cut down by the 1868 treaty, the 1877 Black Hills seizure, the 1889 breakup and the 1910 opening of Bennett County.

name: West Arlington, Jacksonville, FL (tract 155.02)
rule_out: piece of a 1990 tract; generic, thin story
hook: A suburb that grew after the 1953 Mathews Bridge opened, whose apartments and 1967 mall aged as growth moved farther out.

name: Gifford, Indian River County, FL
rule_out: piece of a 2010 tract; would need the Gifford CDP or the old tract outline for a series
hook: A Black citrus-labor town next to wealthy Vero Beach that went without safe tap water until the late 1970s and then saw the county's packinghouses fall from 20 to about 8.

name: South and west Madison, Madison County, FL
rule_out: Madison Correctional Institution holds 1,366 of 5,530 residents (25%); piece of a 1990 tract
hook: A former cotton capital whose poorest tract now counts a state prison as a quarter of its residents.

name: South and east Moultrie, Colquitt County, GA
rule_out: piece of a 1990 tract; thin documentation
hook: A south Georgia packing-plant town, where the former Swift plant closed in 1996, with Black and Latino farm and plant workers living on the same side of town.

name: Springfield, MA: North End (Brightwood, Memorial Square), Metro Center and South End
rule_out: none; cluster spans three neighborhoods, consider trimming to North End tracts 8006-8009
hook: The closing of the nation's first federal armory in 1968 took the city's anchor employer, a 1960s riverfront interstate split a Puerto Rican neighborhood, and a 2011 tornado later hit the South End.

name: Downtown Brockton, MA (Main Street)
rule_out: single tract downtown core; a roughly 130-bed emergency shelter and possible subsidized towers may drive the numbers
hook: The downtown of a former national shoe capital that became the region's place of last resort.

name: Grove Hall, Boston (Roxbury/Dorchester line on Blue Hill Ave)
rule_out: none
hook: A bank-drawn mortgage zone (B-BURG, 1968-72) and the 1967 welfare-office uprising on the same avenue turned over a neighborhood through lending, not a highway or plant closing.

name: Mattapan, Boston (Gladeside / Morton St area)
rule_out: too similar to U064 (same B-BURG story) and least extreme on income and health
hook: A Haitian-American immigrant hub built on the B-BURG turnover.

name: Northeast Rochester, NY: Joseph Ave / North Clinton Ave corridor (La Avenida, Marketview Heights, Upper Falls)
rule_out: none
hook: The blocks where Rochester's 1964 uprising began lost ground as Kodak shed jobs from a 60,000-plus peak in 1982, then became the county's top overdose site.

name: West Side Rochester, NY: Bull's Head, JOSANA, Edgerton, Plymouth-Exchange
rule_out: too similar to U043, same city and Kodak story with a thinner dated record
hook: A former commercial gateway left behind by suburbanization, now a brownfield renewal zone.

name: Northwest One / former Sursum Corda area, Washington, DC
rule_out: stability 0.0 and a tiny tract likely made up of a few subsidized and public housing buildings in a gentrifying area
hook: Remaining subsidized buildings inside a booming district, a displacement story more than a decline story.

name: West Baltimore: Sandtown-Winchester, Harlem Park, Upton, Poppleton
rule_out: none (heavily covered nationally)
hook: Homes were cleared for a highway built 1975-79 and then never connected, and the transit line planned for its median was canceled in 2015 and revived in 2023.

name: Fairhill and West Kensington, North Philadelphia (the Badlands)
rule_out: none, but stability 0.599 (boundaries shifted since 1990) needs a judgment call
hook: A Puerto Rican neighborhood in a former textile mill district that became the East Coast's largest open-air drug market across two drug eras.

name: Fairhill, North Philadelphia (tract 176.02)
rule_out: duplicate of U023 and stability 0.0
hook: No story of its own; it is U023's story on one unstable tract.

name: Somerset borough, Somerset County, PA
rule_out: thin: borough population flat since 1960; tract holds the hospital and likely senior housing, with no documented decline
hook: A stable county seat, not a declining place.

name: Clarksville (west and south side), Red River County, TX
rule_out: none (tract is a piece of a 2010 tract; compare on the old outline or use city and county series)
hook: A small East Texas county seat where a federal court found federal housing money built segregation (Young v. Pierce), after a century of cotton collapse, and where the hospital closed in 2014.

name: Hearne, Robertson County, TX
rule_out: none (piece of a 2010 tract; railroad decline job counts not found)
hook: A plantation and rail-junction town where a 2000 drug sweep built on one informant arrested 27 to 28 mostly Black residents and became an ACLU case.

name: Black Mesa area, Navajo Nation chapters (Pinon, Forest Lake, Whippoorwill, Kayenta, Shonto, Nazlini, Cornfields) and part of the Hopi Reservation, AZ
rule_out: none, but the cluster mixes two nations (Hopi tract 9400.12) and tracts start in 1990
hook: Fifty years of Peabody coal mining on Black Mesa funded Navajo and Hopi budgets while the federal land partition forced families to move, then the mines closed in 2005 and 2019.

name: Tohono O'odham Nation (Sells, Baboquivari and Pisinemo districts), Pima County, AZ
rule_out: none (thin tract-level time series)
hook: A nation split in two by the 1853 border, drawn off its desert farms into cotton wage work, and now living inside a growing border enforcement zone.

name: Central, East and Southeast Bakersfield plus Oildale, Kern County, CA
rule_out: mixed cluster: Oildale and Southeast Bakersfield have different histories; consider splitting
hook: An oil-and-farm-labor city where Dust Bowl migrants, Black families and Mexican American farmworkers each settled into separate, polluted neighborhoods.

name: Skid Row, downtown Los Angeles, CA
rule_out: services district by design (1976 containment plan concentrated shelters and SROs); not a neighborhood decline story
hook: The only candidate whose numbers were set by a deliberate city plan to concentrate homeless services in one place.

name: Jordan Downs, Watts, Los Angeles, CA
rule_out: tract 2421 is a single public housing complex (Jordan Downs, about 700 units, now being rebuilt); rebuild the Watts candidate from several Watts tracts
hook: Strongest LA story: Watts stacks covenants and HOLC, wartime public housing, 1965, South LA plant closures, the I-105, the crack era, 1992 and a Black-to-Latino shift, all dated.

name: East-central Compton near Alameda St and Rosecrans Ave, Compton, CA
rule_out: weak screen fit (17th income and 15th health percentile) and piece of a 1990 tract (stability 0.0)
hook: A suburb that flipped twice: white to Black middle class through blockbusting, then, after plant closures and the crack era, to mostly Latino and low income.

name: West-central Roswell, Chaves County, NM
rule_out: piece of a 1990 tract (stability 0.0); one citywide event with no documented tie to this tract
hook: A small city that lost Walker Air Force Base in 1967 and 14.4% of its population in a decade.

name: Eastern Navajo Nation chapters in New Mexico (Tohatchi, Navajo/Red Lake, Naschitti, Crownpoint area and others), McKinley, San Juan and Sandoval counties, NM
rule_out: none, but the cluster is scattered across three counties (stability 0.342), and the 'Gallup' label is wrong because the city is not included
hook: The uranium legacy: decades of mining left hundreds of abandoned mines near Dine homes, and the tribal sawmill at Navajo, NM, meant as an alternative, closed in the mid-1990s.

name: Western Alabama Black Belt (Marengo, Wilcox, Dallas, Choctaw, Sumter; includes Gee's Bend area)
rule_out: none; but five-county patchwork, consider narrowing to Wilcox and Marengo
hook: The Gee's Bend ferry was shut in 1962 after residents used it to register to vote and did not run again for 44 years, on top of a 70% population loss in Wilcox County since 1900.

name: West Decatur (Moulton Street West), Decatur, AL
rule_out: state work release center (683 people, 10% of cluster) in tract 000600
hook: A 3M PFAS company town where a closed west-side middle school was sold to the polluter, though the PFAS story is citywide, not neighborhood-specific.

name: Odenville area, St. Clair County, AL (tract 040508)
rule_out: no 1990 tract match (piece of a larger 2010 tract) and no documented history
hook: Nothing distinct found; possibly a newer exurban low-income pocket rather than a long decline.

name: Central Talladega (tract 010600), Talladega, AL
rule_out: thin documentation; textile closures UNCONFIRMED
hook: The lowest-income tract in the batch sits in a NASCAR and HBCU town that lost 17% of its people after 1980, but the local causes are not yet documented.

name: Central Tullahoma (tract 970900), Tullahoma, TN
rule_out: thin documentation; town grew every decade, so not a decline story
hook: A poor pocket inside a growing Air Force engineering town, a contrast story rather than a story of many cuts.

name: The Westside (College Hill Courts), Chattanooga, TN
rule_out: public housing (about 629 CHA units, roughly 30% of the tract's 2,070 units) likely drives the numbers
hook: Site of Golden Gateway, the 5th-largest urban renewal project in the U.S. (410 acres), now in the middle of a $1 billion rebuild of 1940 public housing.

name: South Memphis / Soulsville (Stax, Mason Temple, former Foote Homes), Memphis, TN
rule_out: none; overlaps U011, which is the more distinct Memphis pick
hook: Memphis's music and civil-rights landmarks (Stax closed 1975, Mason Temple) sit next to its largest public-housing concentration, which was cleared in 2016-2018.

name: North Memphis (New Chicago, Klondike-Smokey City, south Frayser), Memphis, TN
rule_out: none
hook: The most distinct Memphis pick: Firestone (more than 3,000 workers at its peak) and the South's largest farm-equipment plant closed in 1983 and 1983-85, I-40 cut through Klondike, and Klondike-Smokey City lost 55% of its people from 1980 to 2010.

name: Desha County, AR (Dumas, McGehee, Arkansas City) plus Dermott and Bolivar and Sunflower counties, MS
rule_out: Sunflower MS tract holds 3,094 people in correctional facilities (likely Parchman, 14% of cluster); crosses the river with no bridge; duplicates R030
hook: Delta mechanization and out-migration (Desha down 58% since 1940), plus the Rohwer internment camp, but the story repeats Phillips County's.

name: Helena-West Helena, Elaine and Marianna (Phillips and Lee counties, AR, plus one Coahoma MS tract)
rule_out: none; drop the Coahoma MS tract to keep it in Arkansas
hook: Site of the 1919 Elaine massacre of sharecroppers who were organizing; the county then lost 64% of its people after 1950, and Helena had the steepest population drop of any U.S. metro or micro area in the 2000s.

name: West Louisville (Russell, California, Portland, Algonquin), Louisville, KY
rule_out: none; consider dropping tract 21111005000 (Old Louisville, Spalding University, 164 in college housing)
hook: A thriving Black business district on Walnut Street erased by urban renewal, then the 1968 Parkland unrest and white flight turned the whole West End into a segregated, disinvested area.

name: Old Louisville (southwest part, near Limerick), Louisville, KY
rule_out: college students may drive low income (27% of Old Louisville residents were students in 2000); same city as stronger U015
hook: A Victorian mansion district that slid into rooming houses after the Depression and the 1937 flood, lost 639 buildings to urban renewal, and only partly came back through preservation.

name: Huntington south side and east end (Fairfield, Highlawn and nearby; names unconfirmed), Huntington, WV
rule_out: none; tracts are scattered across the city, consider narrowing to Fairfield tracts 14 and 15
hook: A railroad and factory city that lost 46% of its people after 1950 and became the national face of the fentanyl wave in 2015 and 2016.

name: Downtown New Kensington and Arnold, Westmoreland County, PA
rule_out: none
hook: The birthplace of American aluminum, where Alcoa moved its labs and plant out over four decades (closing in 1971) and both towns lost more than half their people.

name: Franklin (city), Venango County, PA
rule_out: thin documentation; single small tract only trackable from 1990
hook: An oil boom town far from any coal mine that was hit by coal's decline anyway, because its last big employer, Joy, built mining machines.

name: Harlan County coal camps (Lynch, Benham, Cumberland, Evarts, Wallins Creek), KY, with edges in Bell County, KY and Lee County, VA
rule_out: none; consider trimming to Harlan-only tracts (cluster includes Lee County, VA); USP Lee is not in the cluster
hook: The archetype of the coal company town: built by steel companies, fought over in the 1930s mine wars, emptied by mechanization (mine jobs down 82% from 1950 to 1965), and hit by the last mine bankruptcies.

name: Rural Bell County around Middlesboro and Pineville, KY, with edges in Knox, Whitley (KY) and Claiborne (TN)
rule_out: too similar to stronger R015; tract 9611 is 12% incarcerated (likely Bell County Forestry Camp, unconfirmed); may not include Middlesboro city itself
hook: A city built in a meteor crater by British investors as a planned steel town that went bust within five years, then lived and declined on coal.

name: Rural Clay County (south of Manchester) and eastern Knox County (around Barbourville), KY
rule_out: persistent poverty rather than decline (Clay County population down only 15% since 1940); overlaps R015 and R004
hook: The county the New York Times ranked the hardest place to live in America in 2014, where poverty, drug trafficking and vote-buying fed each other for decades.

name: Rural tracts across Owsley, Lee, Wolfe, Breathitt, Magoffin and Jackson counties, KY (Booneville, Campton area)
rule_out: spread across six counties, not one community; recommend narrowing to the Owsley County tract
hook: A farm and tobacco story, not a coal one: Owsley County lost 55% of its people since 1940, and small burley farms lost their cash crop when the federal tobacco program ended.

name: Peach Creek, Crooked Creek and the Guyandotte valley north and east of Logan, Logan County, WV
rule_out: tract boundaries shifted since 1990 (stability 0.725); overlaps R015 coal theme
hook: The rail-yard side of coal: a C&O yard community that moved the Logan coalfield's output and shrank as mine jobs fell 90% from their 1940 peak, with the worst health score in the batch.

name: Highland Park and the Davison corridor (Dexter-Fenkell, Oakman Blvd, Chalfonte, Bethune), Detroit area
rule_out: none, but only 2 of 8 tracts are in Highland Park; re-cut around Highland Park if chosen
hook: A small city that Ford and Chrysler built and then left, ending in state takeover, $17.7M water debt and streetlights pulled in 2011.

name: Detroit Near West Side (Core City, Jeffries/Woodbridge, North Corktown, Midwest, Chadsey-Condon)
rule_out: none; tracts not contiguous, and tract 5218 is dominated by Jeffries/Woodbridge
hook: Land graded 74% HOLC 'D' that then got two freeways and a tower project that was built, imploded and rebuilt as mixed income.

name: Warrendale and Warren Ave corridor, west Detroit
rule_out: thin documentation; weaker than U046 on the public housing angle
hook: Detroit's edge on the Dearborn line, anchored by Herman Gardens (1943, 2,144 units), which turned over to Black and then Arab immigrant families.

name: Riverside Park area, Puritas-Longmead, west Cleveland
rule_out: single tract dominated by Riverside Park HUD-subsidized complex (~497 units)
hook: Not distinct; the numbers reflect one subsidized complex.

name: Central, Kinsman, Fairfax and Hough, Cleveland East Side
rule_out: none; heavy public housing but spread over four estates
hook: The birthplace of US public housing (Outhwaite and Cedar-Central, 1935-37) on 86% HOLC 'D' land, then the 1966 Hough uprising, cut renewal funds and roughly 75% population loss.

name: Arbor Park Village, Central, Cleveland
rule_out: single tract dominated by Arbor Park Village subsidized complex (~488 units); fold into U007
hook: Same Central story as U007, told less well in one tract.

name: Mill Creek valley, Cincinnati (West End, Lower Price Hill-Queensgate, North Fairmount, English Woods, Millvale)
rule_out: none; no Cincinnati HOLC map in Mapping Inequality file, and some tracts are dominated by large subsidized sites
hook: About 27,000 people cleared for I-75 (1959-73) were pushed up a polluted industrial creek valley into public housing that was later torn down, and the city formally apologized in 2023.

name: North Toledo / North End (Vistula, Sherman, Polish Village, North River)
rule_out: none; documentation still thin (web search budget ran out mid-research)
hook: Toledo's oldest settlement and Polish working-class district, wedged between the Libbey glass works and the Jeep Stickney plant (closed 2007).

name: Youngstown inner neighborhoods (North, South, East sides, Brier Hill)
rule_out: none; tracts spread citywide, so consider re-cutting to one side
hook: The steel version: Black Monday (Sept 19, 1977, 5,000 jobs) through about 40,000 lost manufacturing jobs to a city that planned in writing to shrink.

name: West-central Marion, OH (Tract 3)
rule_out: thin documentation; one small tract (prisons are in another tract)
hook: The town whose steam shovels dug the Panama Canal, now reliant on prisons and one appliance plant.

name: Seventh Ward, St. Roch, Florida and Desire areas (New Orleans Upper Ninth and Seventh wards)
rule_out: none; consider dropping outlier tract 17.51 (Viavant/Venetian Isles); Agriculture St landfill is in adjacent tract 137.01, not inside
hook: Strongest New Orleans candidate: a neighborhood hemmed in one layer at a time by the Industrial Canal (1923), a city dump turned housing site, the Florida (1946) and Desire (1956) projects, and the I-10 over Claiborne (1969), with Katrina as the last cut rather than the first.

name: Central City, B.W. Cooper, Gert Town, Hollygrove and Dixon (New Orleans)
rule_out: cluster joins two separate areas; overlaps U012 on public housing
hook: Central City mostly stayed dry in Katrina yet lost 41% of its people from 2000 to 2010, after a half-century slide of its Black main street on Dryades Street and the rise and fall of the Magnolia projects.

name: North Baton Rouge fenceline (Istrouma, Delmont Place, Legion Village, Brookstown, Scotlandville edge)
rule_out: none; tracts 11.03/11.04 (Mid City) are a weaker fit and could be dropped
hook: Strongest Baton Rouge candidate: the 1909 refinery kept growing for a century while the worker housing along its fence turned over, was cut by I-110 (1957-1984), and was partly bought out by ExxonMobil.

name: South Shreveport tract off Mansfield Road (Linwood Ave, W 70s-80s streets; local name unconfirmed)
rule_out: boundaries shifted since 1990 (0.58); single small tract; name and local history unconfirmed
hook: Possibly a postwar south Shreveport neighborhood tied to the old Western Electric (7,500 jobs at peak, closed 2001) and GM (closed 2012) job base, but that link is unconfirmed.

name: North and South Monroe plus West Monroe / Bawcomville
rule_out: mixes Black Monroe neighborhoods with white working-class West Monroe; recommend splitting
hook: Strongest Monroe candidate: the 1916 gas field made Monroe 'the natural gas capital of the world,' then its core thinned (down 17.2% since 1980) as the field played out and families moved to the growing suburbs.

name: Scattered tracts around Monroe and Ruston (south Monroe, Richwood, south Ruston, Columbia, Chatham)
rule_out: not a coherent neighborhood: four parishes, about 60 miles apart
hook: No single story; Richwood or south Ruston might each merit a separate look.

name: Central and South Alexandria (downtown edge, I-49 corridor, south side)
rule_out: none; tract 139 has 237 in corrections (about 10% of tract, under 2% of cluster); neighborhood names unconfirmed
hook: A wartime military town whose air base closed in 1992 and whose I-49 segment, the last gap in the interstate, opened through the city in 1996.

name: Claiborne and Union parishes (Homer, Haynesville, Athens, Farmerville, Bernice)
rule_out: none; 3 of 8 tracts are in Union Parish, not Claiborne; David Wade prison appears to lie outside these tracts
hook: Two energy booms a century apart: the 1921 oil strike that built Homer and Haynesville, and the 2008 Haynesville Shale gas boom that did not stop a parish that has lost 56% of its people since 1930.

name: Winnsboro, Franklin Parish
rule_out: too similar to U041 (Rayville); pick one
hook: A Delta parish seat where a private segregation academy opened weeks after the 1970 school desegregation order, on top of a 38.9% parish population loss since 1940.

name: Rayville, Richland Parish
rule_out: too similar to R016 (Winnsboro); labeled urban but is a small rural town
hook: A Delta cotton town whose abandoned farmland now hosts Meta's Hyperion data center (2024), which raises the question of whether new investment reaches residents with the worst health.

name: Clarksdale, Coahoma County, MS
rule_out: none (DELTA PICK; note it is coded micro, not rural)
hook: The first cotton crop planted, picked and baled entirely by machine was grown at Hopson Plantation just south of town in 1944, and the 1967 Senate hunger tour ended in Clarksdale; the county has lost 57% of its people since 1950, and the tracts line up perfectly back to 1990.

name: Belzoni, Humphreys County, MS
rule_out: none, but recheck: ACS 2020-24 poverty (15.7%) clashes with 41.6% in 2008-12; overlaps Clarksdale on cotton
hook: Catfish replaced cotton as the Delta's work, then imports helped cut Mississippi pond acreage 67% (2001-2015), and the county hospital closed in 2013; the county has lost 70% of its people since 1940.

name: Indianola and rural Sunflower County (with pieces of Bolivar, Leflore, Washington), MS
rule_out: spans 4 counties; boundaries shifted (0.763); 732 incarcerated people; overlaps Clarksdale. Re-cut to Indianola only if wanted
hook: The first Citizens' Council formed in Indianola in 1954 and Fannie Lou Hamer was fired near Ruleville in 1962; later the Delta Pride catfish plant brought 1,000 jobs, a 1990 strike, and a 2011 closure.

name: Lower Delta river counties: Lake Providence (East Carroll, LA), Eudora (Chicot, AR), Sharkey, Issaquena, rural Humphreys and Holmes, MS
rule_out: not one place (3 states, 6 counties); Issaquena tract is 37% prison; duplicates Clarksdale and Belzoni. Lake Providence alone could be re-cut
hook: These are the emptiest river counties, where Issaquena had the state's highest share of enslaved people in 1860 and is now its smallest county, bracketed by the 1927 flood and the 2023 Rolling Fork tornado.

name: Meadville and Bude, Franklin County, MS
rule_out: piece of a split 2010 tract with no 1990 match; small; decline undocumented; not Delta
hook: A hill-country timber and furniture county, not a cotton one, where the 1964 Klan murders of Henry Dee and Charles Moore are well documented but the job losses are not.

name: Crowley (north, west and south sides), Acadia Parish, LA
rule_out: thin documentation; boundaries shifted (0.743)
hook: A Cajun prairie rice town where tract poverty rose from 39% to 47% since 1990, but the causes are not yet sourced.

name: Marksville, Mansura, Cottonport, Bunkie and Simmesport, Avoyelles Parish, LA (plus Morganza)
rule_out: state prison (Raymond Laborde CC) is 44% of one tract and about 8% of the cluster with a jail; multi-town spread; decline undocumented
hook: A French-Catholic cotton parish where the state prison became a main presence, with the Morganza Spillway openings and a 1994 tribal casino on the other side of the ledger.

name: Shreveport's old Black core: Ledbetter Heights (the Bottoms), Allendale, Lakeside, Stoner Hill, MLK/Cooper Road area, plus old Bossier City
rule_out: drop tract 246.02 (1,214 incarcerated, 6% of cluster) and the Bossier City tract; overlaps U014 on oil and GM
hook: Lead Belly's Bottoms, graded D in the 1930s, then public housing, demolitions and I-20, an oil bust, and the Western Electric (2001) and GM (2012) closures; half the people left and poverty has stayed near 48% for 50 years.

name: Cedar Grove and nearby south Shreveport (Sunset Acres/Caddo Heights area), LA
rule_out: none; boundaries shifted (0.798) is a judgment call; choose one Shreveport story
hook: A working-class area that was not poor in 1970 and turned fast: poverty went from 17% to 38% and the Black share from 28% to 65% by 1990, with a two-day riot in 1988 and later plant closures.

name: East and central North Little Rock, plus Little Rock east of I-30 and the airport tract, AR
rule_out: crosses the river and two cities and includes an airport tract; local history unconfirmed
hook: The poor side of a twin city, where HOLC D grades cover up to half of some tracts and the population fell 51% since 1970, but the rail-town angle is still unconfirmed.

name: Ohio River Bend towns (Middleport, Pomeroy, Racine, Rutland), Meigs County OH, plus Ravenswood, Jackson County WV
rule_out: none; the cluster crosses a state line, so the WV tract (Ravenswood aluminum) may split the story
hook: A 150-year slide in coal and salt river towns, where the last lift, a 1957 aluminum plant across the river, closed in 2015 with 650 jobs.

name: West Dayton (with Drexel and south Trotwood), Montgomery County OH
rule_out: none
hook: Each cut is a separate dated event on one timeline: HOLC C and D grades, the 1966 unrest, US-35 taking 283 homes, the Delphi and GM closings, NCR leaving in 2009, the 2017 overdose peak and the 2018 loss of the only west side hospital.

name: Central and South Akron along the Innerbelt (Summit Lake, South Akron, downtown edge), Summit County OH
rule_out: none; the Summit County Jail is in tract 5068 (539 people, about 4% of the cluster), and tracts 5066 and 5086 were HOLC A or B, so consider trimming them
hook: The Rubber Capital lost its tire plants, and a highway built through its neighborhoods (1968 to 1986) was closed and is now being handed back as empty land.

name: North end of Clinton (between downtown and Lyons), Clinton County IA
rule_out: single tract with thin documentation of local closures
hook: A former lumber capital that had a second, factory-era peak in 1970 and lost almost a third of its people after that.

name: Pana, Christian County IL
rule_out: single tract; causes of decline after 1960 are undocumented
hook: A coal and rose-greenhouse town with a violent 1899 mine war in its past.

name: Englewood and Fuller Park, Chicago (plus Wentworth Gardens tract), Cook County IL
rule_out: none; tract 3406 is mostly the Wentworth Gardens public housing complex (about 7% of the cluster), so consider dropping it; the story overlaps U063 and U065
hook: The Dan Ryan Expressway and the 1971 stockyard closing split Fuller Park, while Englewood's 63rd and Halsted shopping hub emptied out; it is the best documented of the three Chicago seeds and also the most familiar.

name: Woodlawn (with west edge of Washington Park), Chicago, Cook County IL
rule_out: none; numbers are less extreme and the latest chapter is reinvestment
hook: The most distinct of the three Chicago seeds: a neighborhood shaped for 70 years by a large institution next door, from university renewal in the 1950s to mass arson, the 1996 Green Line cut and the Obama Center opening in 2026.

name: West Garfield Park (K-Town area), Chicago, Cook County IL
rule_out: one small tract (about 1,050 to 1,200 people) with milder numbers (income pctile 14.4) and a story that repeats Englewood's
hook: The April 1968 riots left rubble along three miles of Madison Street, and many of those lots are still empty.

name: Watseka, Iroquois County IL
rule_out: thin documentation; no dated compounding causes found
hook: A farm county seat that started shrinking only after 2000; nothing found makes it stand out from other Midwest farm towns.

name: South Side (61605) and riverfront, Peoria, Peoria County IL
rule_out: none; check for public housing in tract 16 (possibly Taft Homes) and a 197-person correctional site in tract 12
hook: A one-company town where Caterpillar's 1980s crisis, two long strikes and the 2017 headquarters move hit a South Side that HOLC had mostly graded D.
